tw-screen.label: Keep the screen always on
tw-screen.info: The TV should not switch itself off while you are watching.

tw-battery.label: Protect the battery (charge up to 85%)
tw-battery.info: Plugged in around the clock, a phone wears its battery out fast. This One UI setting caps the charge at 85%, greatly extending its life.

tw-dnd.label: Do not disturb (TV mode)
tw-dnd.info: Silences notifications and calls that would pop up on the TV, over your content and in front of everyone.

tw-updates.label: Turn off automatic updates
tw-updates.info: A system update can undo the whole setup. To be safe, keep the device as it is.

tw-anim.label: Reduce animations
tw-anim.info: Faster, more direct navigation on the big screen.

tw-font.label: Larger font (TV default)
tw-font.info: Bigger text for comfortable reading from the couch.

tw-font-big.label: Much larger font
tw-font-big.info: For smaller TVs or couches further away.

tw-font-normal.label: Normal font size
tw-font-normal.info: Returns the font to the phone's default size, if the larger options don't work for you.

tw-rotate.label: Force landscape orientation
tw-rotate.info: Keeps everything in landscape on the TV, even apps that would open upright. If the screen ends up the wrong way round, use the "Rotate screen" button on the remote until it's right.

tw-gestures.label: Gesture navigation
tw-gestures.info: Swaps the buttons for gestures, freeing up screen space.

tw-lock.label: Remove the screen lock
tw-lock.info: Goes straight to your content, without asking for a password via the remote.

tw-home.label: Use the TV launcher as default
tw-home.info: The phone opens straight into the TV screen, not into Android.

tw-res-fhd.label: Full HD resolution (1080p)
tw-res-fhd.info: For Full HD TVs (1920x1080). The most common resolution.

tw-res-4k.label: 4K resolution (2160p)
tw-res-4k.info: For 4K/UHD TVs (3840x2160). Only use this if the TV really is 4K.

tw-dpi-default.label: Default interface size
tw-dpi-default.info: Text, icons and menus at the right scale for the chosen resolution — the TV standard.

tw-dpi-small.label: Smaller interface
tw-dpi-small.info: Text, icons and menus 20% smaller, for those who prefer more content on screen.

tw-dpi-large.label: Larger interface
tw-dpi-large.info: Text, icons and menus 20% larger — easier to read from a distance.

tw-sound.label: Mute touch sounds
tw-sound.info: No click on every tap — better for the living room.

adbMissing.title: A program component is missing
adbMissing.message: DexArmor needs an internal component (ADB) to talk to your Galaxy, and it could not be found. This usually means an incomplete installation, or a file removed by antivirus software.
steps: Close DexArmor and open it again — sometimes that is enough.
If it persists, reinstall the program from the original installer.
If you use antivirus software, check its quarantine: some remove DexArmor components by mistake.

noDevices.title: No Galaxy detected
noDevices.message: The computer is not seeing any device.
steps: Make sure the cable is connected — and that it is a DATA cable, not just a charging one.
Turn on USB Debugging: Settings → Developer options → USB debugging.
If Developer options are not there: Settings → About phone → tap "Build number" 7 times.
On Windows, install the Samsung USB driver if the device does not show up.

noPermissions.title: No permission to access the device
noPermissions.message: The computer detected the Galaxy but cannot reach it. This is usually a stuck ADB service or a missing/outdated USB driver (Windows).
steps: Hold on — DexArmor will restart the ADB service automatically.
On Windows: reinstall the Samsung USB driver and try again.
On Mac/Linux: reconnect the cable after the service restarts.

offline.title: Device is not responding
offline.message: The Galaxy shows up but is not responding to commands. Usually it is a stuck ADB service, a bad cable, or the device in an odd state.
steps: Hold on — DexArmor will restart the connection automatically.
If it persists, change the USB cable or the computer port.
Unplug and reconnect the phone.

offlineWireless.title: No contact over the network
offlineWireless.message: Your Galaxy is paired over Wi-Fi but stopped responding. This is almost always a network hiccup — it comes back on its own once the device reappears.
steps: Check that the device is still on and on the same Wi-Fi network as this computer.
If it is in airplane mode or has Wi-Fi off, just turn it back on.
The connection restores itself — you do not need to reconnect anything by hand.
If it takes too long, plug in the USB cable: it works even with the network down.

otherMode.title: Phone in a special mode
otherMode.message: The Galaxy is in a mode that does not allow setup right now (recovery, bootloader or similar).
steps: Restart the phone normally until Android has loaded.
Reconnect and try again.

ready.title: Galaxy ready
ready.message: Device authorized and responding. You can start the setup.

unauthorized.title: Authorize the computer on the phone
unauthorized.message: DexArmor found your Galaxy, but it does not trust this computer yet. That is normal on the first connection.
steps: Unlock your Galaxy's screen (the prompt only appears with the screen unlocked).
Tap "Allow" on the "Allow USB debugging?" prompt.
Tick "Always allow from this computer" before tapping Allow.
If the prompt does not appear: pull down the notification bar and change the USB mode from "Charging only" to "File transfer (MTP)".

unknown.title: Unrecognized state
unknown.message: The device returned a state DexArmor does not know yet. Restart the phone and the connection, then try again.
steps: Unplug and reconnect the phone.
Restart the device if the problem continues.

firstGuide.title: Welcome to DexArmor
firstGuide.intro: Before you start, it's worth understanding the right way to use the program — 2 minutes that save you trouble later.

s1.title: 1. Build the TV setup first
s1.body: Use the Recommended setup and adjust resolution, interface size, font and rotation until the picture looks perfect on YOUR TV. Interface settings can be redone as many times as you need at this stage.

s2.title: 2. Got it right? Save it and stay there
s2.body: Once the interface is the way you want it, save it as a profile (Profiles tab). From then on, avoid fiddling with the interface settings: many repeated changes can stack on top of each other and disrupt switching between phone and TV modes.

s3.title: 3. Then feed the setup
s3.body: Day to day is about adding content, not changing the interface: drag apps (.apk), films, music and ROMs straight onto the DexArmor window — they go to the phone right away. The program ships no third-party apps: the ones you want, you install.

s4.title: 4. If the phone screen goes odd
s4.body: Went back to phone mode and the interface looks strange? Use "Restore the phone interface" in the left column — it restores the original interface without deleting anything on the device or your TV mode.

dex.intro: Some Samsung devices have DeX mode. When you plug into HDMI, DeX opens on its own and takes over the screen — which gets in the way of the TV experience we just built.

dexMode.title: DeX mode
dexMode.desc: Opens a desktop much like a computer's. Built for productivity, with windows and a mouse — not for watching TV from the couch.

tvMode.title: TV experience
tvMode.desc: Opens straight into the TV launcher, with simple remote navigation. This is what we want to use the device as a TV box.

dex.conclusion: So on devices with DeX, its automatic launch has to be turned off. With DeX out of the way, the phone opens straight into the TV interface when plugged into HDMI.
dex.note: Option names can vary a little by model and version. If you can't find it through the path above, search for "DeX" in the Settings search.
dex.hdmiWarning: The DeX menu only appears in settings once the device is already connected to the TV over HDMI. Without the cable plugged in, the option is unavailable — which is why this step is best done at the end, with the phone already on the TV.

s1.title: Open Settings
s1.body: On the phone, go to Settings › Connected devices.

s3.title: Turn off automatic launch
s3.body: Turn off "Start automatically when HDMI is connected".

s4.title: Done
s4.body: Now, when you plug into HDMI, the device opens the TV interface instead of DeX.

s1.title: Open Settings
s1.body: On the phone, go to Settings › Connected devices › Samsung DeX.

s3.title: Choose "Mirror"
s3.body: Select "Mirror" instead of "Extend". Mirror opens the TV interface; extend opens DeX.

s4.title: Done
s4.body: The device now mirrors the screen when plugged into HDMI, opening straight into the TV launcher.

nodex.label: My device has no DeX
nodex.hint: E.g. Galaxy Z Flip and entry-level models

s1.title: Nothing to do
s1.body: Without DeX, the device already opens straight into the TV interface over HDMI. You can skip this step.

sideload.title: Install apps and send files
sideload.intro: DexArmor turns the phone into a TV, but it does not come with third-party apps: streaming, browsers, games and emulators are your choice. Installing any of them takes seconds — just drag and drop.

s1.title: 1. Have the file on the computer
s1.body: An Android app is a .apk file. Download it from a trusted source (the phone's own app store, the app's official site, or well-known repositories) and keep it handy.

s2.title: 2. Drag it onto the DexArmor window
s2.body: With the phone connected, drag the file anywhere onto this window. The whole screen becomes a drop area with the possible targets — nothing to open beforehand.

s3.title: 3. Drop it on "Install on the phone"
s3.body: That's the large target at the top, for .apk files. The app is installed straight onto the device and shows up in the TV launcher alongside the others.

s4.title: 4. Files go on the targets below
s4.body: Films, music, ROMs and general files: drop them on the matching folder (Movies, Music, Game ROMs, Downloads). Several at once works too, with progress and the option to cancel.

notes: On the first install, Android may ask for a confirmation on the phone screen. That's normal: allow it and DexArmor carries on from there.
.apkm and .xapk files (multi-part packages) are accepted too.
Out of space on the phone? DexArmor warns you before starting — use Cleanup, in the right-hand column, and try again.
